title: Pricing callable bonds and optimal callable time under the fractional Black-Scholes market: L1 consistency of the deep-learning price estimator (Theorem 3.6)
author: Yuecai Han, Yinong Wu, Xudong Zheng
work: Pricing callable bonds and optimal callable time under the Fractional Black-Scholes market
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 09, pp. 1--13; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.09; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the headline consistency result of the article: the deep-learning estimator of the callable-bond price in a discretised fractional Black-Scholes market converges in L1 to the true price. Its complete proof has to pass from the almost-sure convergence of the discretised expectation by the strong law of large numbers and dominated convergence, rewrite the estimator as an empirical average over the same path grid, isolate the event on which the estimated call time differs from the true one, and then transfer that stopping-time error into a price error by Cauchy-Schwarz against the square-integrability of the discounted payoff, invoking the source-local convergence of the estimated optimal call time. The mechanism is research level because the chain has to control conditional distribution estimators of a fractional-Brownian-motion discrete scheme uniformly in the state, remove the a priori boundedness of the price by a truncation argument and propagate the one-step error backwards through the Bermudan recursion before the final stopping-time comparison is available. It is graded H2 rather than H3 because each ingredient is a quantitative convergence estimate rather than a new structural mechanism: the counted body itself performs the final assembly of prerequisites that the delivered item retains uncounted as complete context.
